title: ExpertPlex: A High-Goodput Disaggregated Serving System for MoE LLMs with Adaptive Persistent Kernels
event_hint: ExpertPlex: MoE LLM serving system with hybrid disaggregation-colocation architecture
problem: MoE LLMs have massive weights (95-98% of parameters) and dynamic computation that impede efficient serving. Existing instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) isolates phases on separate full-model replicas, each spanning tens to hundreds of GPUs, making resource allocation increasingly coarse. Configured prefill-to-decode ratios often mismatch demand. Prefill-decode colocation solutions using Green Context partition each GPU by phase and fix phase resources during a kernel, unable to track resource changes across operations or layerwise variation in routed expert load, causing head-of-line blocking or idle reserved resources.
mechanism: Hybrid disaggregation-colocation architecture that shares massive MoE experts across phases while disaggregating lightweight attention modules. Expert sharing eliminates over 95% of duplicate model weights and multiplexes dynamically sparse computation, while attention disaggregation reduces attention communication cost. Uses (1) Adaptive Persistent Kernels (APK) to schedule dynamic expert computation at tile granularity for efficient, isolated execution; (2) attention-initiated MoE communication to avoid network interference and enable cross-phase communication-computation overlap; (3) a tile-to-cluster model to optimize these mechanisms for maximum goodput.

evidence.claim: Goodput improvement over instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation
evidence.condition: Serving MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.1-FP8 on real-world workloads
Serving MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.1-FP8 on real-world workloads

evidence.claim: Expert sharing eliminates duplicate model weights
evidence.condition: Hybrid architecture sharing MoE experts across phases

evidence.claim: MoE weights contribute to model parameters (DeepSeek-V4-Pro)

evaluation_context: Evaluated serving two frontier MoE LLMs (MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.1-FP8) on real-world workloads. Compared against instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation and Green Context-based prefill-decode colocation. Uses expert parallelism (EP) to shard experts across GPUs with all-to-all communication for dispatch and combine operations. Attention uses data parallelism (DP) or tensor parallelism (TP).
limitations: Evidence pack limited to abstract, introduction, and background sections. Detailed experimental methodology, specific hardware configurations, workload characteristics, baseline implementation details, and comprehensive performance metrics (TTFT, TPOT, latency percentiles) not visible in front evidence. Claims of 2.01x and 1.66x goodput improvements lack supporting experimental conditions and configurations in visible text.
project_relevance: Relevant to TPN's focus on network awareness of inference stages and KV cache positioning. ExpertPlex introduces attention-initiated one-sided MoE communication that uses mostly disjoint network paths to transfer activations between attention and MoE-side buffers, reducing cross-phase network interference. The architecture enables cross-phase communication-computation overlap, addressing TPN's concern about network-side optimization value relative to pure GPU memory scheduling. However, evidence pack does not show explicit network-awareness of inference stages or token performance targets, nor does it present TTFT/TPOT/network utilization metrics that TNP prioritizes.
